mode: new ui-mockup using Section 2 as style reference
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: one high-fidelity desktop website Section 3 visual for NSEDU, a student college-discovery platform in India. Generate a new section, not a hero or a full homepage.
Input image: the provided local Section 2 screenshot is ONLY a brand/style reference. Continue its ivory, wine and taupe editorial theme, real serif/sans hierarchy, thin borders and restrained spacing. Replace the city/state content completely with a course-wise college discovery table.

Create ONE complete landscape 1900-by-1100-ish composition, front-facing flat UI screenshot, crisp readable typography, expertly aligned columns, all five rows and footer visible. No device frame, perspective, mood board or design annotations. High-end professional editorial product UI; useful and compact, attractive through typography and alignment, not decoration.

Palette: warm ivory #FFFAF8 page, white #FFFFFF rows, wine #72243B headings/active tabs/primary controls, taupe #806C60 secondary elements, pale greige #F1ECE8 secondary controls, dark #2A2024 text, #68636E muted text and #E8D7DC delicate borders. Match DM Serif Display heading/college-name character and Plus Jakarta Sans body/control character. Background nearly plain light ivory with extremely faint corner contour lines only. NO blue, neon, heavy shadows, glossy glass, big campus background illustration, sponsored banners or adverts.

Top, left aligned: elegant modest-sized serif heading EXACTLY "Course-wise colleges in India". Under it EXACTLY "Explore fees, placements and reviews for your preferred course." Upper right, underlined wine action "View all colleges" and arrow, with a small unobtrusive outlined badge "Static demo data".
Second line: a single row of tidy course tabs: "B.Tech" (active filled wine), "MBA", "MBBS", "B.Com", "BBA", "BCA", "B.Des", "M.Tech", "B.Pharm", "Law", "Nursing", "More". Inactive tabs have ivory/greige backgrounds and light borders, not giant tiles. No ugly scrollbar.
Immediately below, a compact preference toolbar: left "B.Tech colleges" with smaller "5 sample colleges"; right three small dropdown controls "Location: All India", "Annual fee: Any budget", "Sort: Default". All modest, compact and aligned.

Main visual: five horizontally aligned white row cards/table rows, restrained 12px radius, hairline border, extremely soft shadow, subtle gap of 8px between rows. All columns align perfectly to one calm pale-greige header strip.
Columns EXACTLY: "#" | "College" | "Annual tuition" | "Placements" | "Demo rating" | "Actions".
Placement header includes tiny "(2024–25)" and tuition header tiny "(2026–27)". Row numbers are list positions, NOT a claimed official rank.
College column: small 58px tasteful rounded campus-photo thumbnail, readable dark serif institution name, city/state beneath in muted sans serif, small "B.Tech" label. Tiny outline heart to save next to the name, no invented accreditation seals or badges.
Tuition column: one clear INR figure per year. No total-course ambiguity.
Placement column: bolder MEDIAN salary first; smaller HIGHEST salary underneath. Both in INR lakhs per annum (LPA), never use placement percentages.
Rating column: one small wine outline star and a readable score out of five; NOT a large arc of yellow stars, NO fabricated review counts.
Actions: checkbox with "Compare", one tidy wine-filled "View details" button with arrow, small secondary "Apply now" text link beneath. Keep the actions in the right column, don't scatter competing CTAs.

Render precisely this fictional static sample dataset, not real IITs or real institutional logos:
01, "Northfield Institute of Technology", "Bengaluru, Karnataka", annual tuition "₹2,40,000 / year", placement "Median ₹8.4 LPA" and "Highest ₹22 LPA", demo rating "4.3 / 5"; compare checkbox CHECKED.
02, "Meadow Engineering College", "Pune, Maharashtra", annual tuition "₹1,80,000 / year", placement "Median ₹6.8 LPA" and "Highest ₹18 LPA", demo rating "4.2 / 5"; compare checkbox unchecked.
03, "Central Institute of Technology", "Hyderabad, Telangana", annual tuition "₹2,10,000 / year", placement "Median ₹7.6 LPA" and "Highest ₹20 LPA", demo rating "4.4 / 5"; compare checkbox CHECKED.
04, "Riverside University", "Chennai, Tamil Nadu", annual tuition "₹1,60,000 / year", placement "Median ₹6.2 LPA" and "Highest ₹16 LPA", demo rating "4.1 / 5"; compare unchecked.
05, "Hillside Engineering Institute", "Delhi NCR", annual tuition "₹2,20,000 / year", placement "Median ₹7.8 LPA" and "Highest ₹21 LPA", demo rating "4.3 / 5"; compare unchecked.
Rows 01 and 03 have a subtle wine border/selection indicator, not a heavy tinted fill.

Under the five rows, a compact contained comparison bar in very pale greige, same width as the table, about 55px high: comparison icon, "2 colleges selected", small "Northfield · Central" labels, right a "Clear" text action and wine-filled "Compare colleges" button with arrow. No floating overlay covering rows.
Small legible footer EXACTLY: "Illustrative colleges and values • Not a ranking • Tuition excludes hostel/living costs."
Small outer footer note "NSEDU · Section 3 concept". The words Static demo data and the illustrative footer MUST be clear and readable.

Visual priorities: highly professional clean table layout; enough space for college names and long labels; consistent compact button dimensions; no cramped text or giant typography; useful student-facing details and scanability. Do not show the site header, first hero, city rows, state rows, a footer menu or unrelated sections. This is only Section 3, ready for design approval before implementation.
